clue.text: Crop to the east of flat field

indicators.note: in an across entry east is to the right, so the crop word follows the flat word

parts.note: a pad is a flat, a place to live
to dock is to crop or cut short, as with a tail

explanation.surface: A harvest growing beside a flat field.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, usually for horses.

clue.text: Back one's claim and eat bread?

definitions.meaning: to support one's words with action or cash
bread is slang for ..., so taking it into one's mouth is a literal reading

explanation.surface: Backing up a claim and having a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prove one's sincerity by spending, and literally describes swallowing money.

clue.text: Infernal pronouncement from the motherland?

definitions.meaning: a sentence condemning someone to hell
punningly, of a nation of mothers, a dam being a mother animal

explanation.surface: A curse from one's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as DAM NATION: a dam is a mother animal, so the whole is a 'mother nation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to eternal punishment in hell, an infernal sentence.

clue.text: Cricket side all padded up for the opening attack

parts.note: the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field
a batsman padded up is set, ready to go in

explanation.surface: A cricket team kitted out for the first assault.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, batsmen wear leg pads; 'padded up' means ready to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the start or first assault of something.

clue.text: Having not much of an inclinaton to possess intelligence, a smart aleck

indicators.note: possess means hold, so the small hill holds the next pieces

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill, only a slight slope (the clue misspells inclination)
wit means intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone with little leaning towards brains is a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is only a link; the slight slope is the wordplay's container.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-it-all is an irritating person who acts as if they have all the answers, a smart aleck.

clue.text: Back pockets reserve a place for waiters

indicators.note: back here tells us to read the whole string of pieces from end to start

parts.note: pots are the pockets on a snooker table
a sub, short for substitute, is a reserve player

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a seat reserved by stuffing their back pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the run POTS + SUB into BUSSTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: People queueing for a bus are waiters, and they wait at this roadside spot.

clue.text: Ask round government department to create confusion

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the ask word goes around the department

parts.note: beg means ask
FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department

explanation.surface: Lobbying a ministry to stir up chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to cloud or obscure, making things confused.

clue.text: Sort items out, most foul

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clear out the worst of the junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormiest describes the foulest weather, so the superlative means most foul.

clue.text: European city where one breaks wind

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the one letter goes inside

parts.note: to wind is to turn
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A city where somebody passes wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy.

clue.text: Drunken soak the wrong way round clings to donkey, or not!

indicators.note: clings to means hugs, so the reversed word wraps round the rest
the wrong way round means reversed, so the soak word is read backwards

parts.note: to dip is to soak briefly

indicators.note: not means take away the word or from the donkey's name

parts.note: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A drunk clinging to a donkey, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or not' means remove the word OR itself from the donkey's name, not a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal for very drunk.

clue.text: Almost reverse Jewish experiences

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the shortened word backwards
almost signals dropping the final letter of the word

parts.note: a Semite is a member of a people including Jews, so the word stands for a Jewish person

explanation.surface: A remark about Jewish experiences being nearly turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts SEMITE to SEMIT; 'reverse' turns that into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Times as a plural noun means experiences, as in having good times or hard times.

clue.text: Maintaining frequency, naturally lost

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the phrase for naturally keeps the frequency letter inside it

parts.note: of course means naturally, as a matter of course

explanation.surface: Keeping a regular rhythm comes naturally to someone otherwise adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes into OF COURSE, after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or traveller off course has strayed from the route, so is lost.

clue.text: Narrow escape from northern land in Greenland's capital

parts.note: earth means land or ground

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so we take the first letter of Greenland

explanation.surface: A lucky escape from an Arctic land, reached in Greenland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is an idiom for a close shave, something only just avoided.

clue.text: See 1 down
Author quick to get the bird

definitions.meaning: a fast-flying bird like a martin, with long scythe wings

explanation.surface: A writer hurries to fetch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: the Irish satirist, an adjective for fast, and a dark aerial bird.

clue.text: Saint given 7 Shroud, needing second to change sheet

indicators.note: shroud means wrap around, so the altered city surrounds the saint
the second letter of the city name must be altered, here becoming A

parts.note: the answer to clue 7 down is the Italian city Turin
Paul is the apostle Saint Paul

explanation.surface: A saint with the Turin Shroud, which needs a change to become a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turin Shroud is a famous relic; here 'Shroud' is a verb, wrapping the altered city round the saint, whose U becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof sheet used as a cover.

clue.text: A 4 previously referred to

parts.note: read the answer as A, then FORE with SAID after it, signalling that it sounds like four: so it spells out A and the figure 4

explanation.surface: A document numbered four was mentioned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as instructions says: A, then a word said aloud like 'four', which gives the clue's 'A 4'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is a formal legal word for something mentioned earlier in a text.

clue.text: Order right, I bet, given cost of delivery

indicators.note: order means arrange, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Placing a bet on what a delivery will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetric relates to childbirth, the delivery of babies.

clue.text: A train crashing into another vehicle losing its first engine part

indicators.note: crashing means smashed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the vehicle word loses its first letter

parts.note: a bike is another vehicle

explanation.surface: A train crashes into another vehicle and loses its lead engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing its first' cuts BIKE to IKE; 'crashing' shuffles A TRAIN with IKE.
explanation.definitionFit: An air intake is the opening through which an engine draws in air.

clue.text: One primate trains others

parts.note: a man is one kind of primate
drills means trains or exercises

explanation.surface: A man, himself a primate, puts other people through their training.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'others': other primates, set against man in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrills are large West African baboons, primates other than humans.

clue.text: See 1
Good teachings rejecting bad woman (student dismissed)

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the word is read backwards
L for learner is the student letter, and it is sent away

parts.note: a harlot is a disreputable woman, a prostitute

explanation.surface: Moral teaching spurns a bad woman, and a student is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'student dismissed' takes L from HARLOT, giving HAROT; 'rejecting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Torah is the body of Jewish law and teaching, held to be the good word of scripture.

clue.text: Save Man United!

definitions.meaning: to use sparingly, as in conserving resources

explanation.surface: A football fan's plea for Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband is to economise; a husband is a married man.

clue.text: Super outlet, great in regular locations

indicators.note: letters at regular positions, every other one, are taken from these words

explanation.surface: A super outlet store, great and found in many towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and so on of OUTLETGREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as a prefix or adjective means extreme or beyond, much like super.

clue.text: A six-footer standing in skimpy attire

indicators.note: standing means upright, so in a down entry the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gnat is an insect, which has six legs

explanation.surface: A tall man in very little clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns A GNAT upside down in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a very skimpy bikini or briefs.

clue.text: See 1 down
He composed the composer's "Unfinished"

indicators.note: unfinished means cut off the last letter

parts.note: Anton Webern was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A composer known for writing an Unfinished symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes on 'Unfinished' suggest Schubert's symphony, but the word just signals cutting the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer of operas such as Der Freischutz.

clue.text: Prompt, though waiting for 3 1/2 minutes?

definitions.meaning: a boiled egg cooking on the stove for a few minutes

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone while timing breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to urge; an egg on the boil is waiting for minutes.

clue.text: Composer aired some music, which Merckx grasped onto

indicators.note: aired means broadcast or spoken, so the composer's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah
a bar is a short section of music

explanation.surface: A composer's music was played while a cyclist held on.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy Merckx was a great Belgian racing cyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist grips the handlebar to steer, so it is what Merckx held onto.

clue.text: Though a navy, it's landlocked

indicators.note: landlocked means enclosed by land, so the country sits enclosed within these words

explanation.surface: A country has a navy despite being without a coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is in fact coastal; it is 'landlocked' only inside the words thouGH A NAvy.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'it' is the West African country itself, the subject of the sentence.

clue.text: Tool box contains not a thing — nothing less

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so the box word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: less means minus, so the nothing letter is taken away

parts.note: none means not a thing
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A toolbox is empty, minus even nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool box' looks like one item, but 'Tool' is the definition and 'box' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a tool for turning nuts, called a wrench in the US.

clue.text: Fight with nurse after party

indicators.note: after puts the nurse word behind the party word

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative party
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Fighting with a nurse after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to compete or struggle, as in contending for a title.
